name: MSC Air Cargo: yellow and black sweeps
description: White 777 freighter with two sweeping lines along the fuselage: a thin black line from just behind the nose, under the cockpit, curving up to run just under the crown back to the fin's root, and below it a broader yellow line from under the nose that sweeps up behind the wing and tapers out over the rear fuselage. The fin white with a yellow band down its trailing edge, widening to the root, edged on its forward side by a thin black line that runs up to the fin's top trailing corner; the black 'msc' logo (m over sc, a wave line between) in the fin's middle. 'MSC AIR CARGO' in black capitals ahead of the wing behind the forward door. White engines.

notes: Measured on I-MSCA (777F, right side flipped, Liège, June 2026) fitted to the 777F shape; N709GT (2024, left) and N707GT (2024) wear the same. The airline was AlisCargo Airlines until 5 September 2024 (STAT Times) and is now MSC Air, but the aircraft are titled 'MSC AIR CARGO' in every photo from 2024 to 2026, and no AlisCargo-titled 777F appears on Commons. The yellow line is about 0.3 m deep under the cockpit, widest (about 0.6 m) behind the wing, and tapers to a point at x 0.84; the black line is about 0.15 m deep. Between them the white gap widens to about 1.5 m mid-body. The title runs x 0.13-0.258, baseline y 0.155, capitals to 0.31. The fin's yellow starts at the root from x 0.25 back; the black line from near the root's leading edge to the top trailing corner. A small Italian flag before the registration is not drawn. The Atlas Air-operated 777Fs N707GT, N708GT and N709GT fly in this scheme for MSC (tagged under GTI).
history: New 2026-11-22 (the maintainer's spotting). MSC Air was AlisCargo Airlines until 5 September 2024.
